reply.thought: Before paying anyone I need to check Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll start by listing the refunds.
The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff exactly, so the next check is the orders, to confirm which customers are in the batch and that the refunds fit against them.
The refunds match Alpha's handoff, and each refunded order belongs to a customer in the batch with enough order value to cover its refund. Next I'll get the net balance for the first customer, acme.
Acme's net of 25415 matches my own check: orders 33101 + 24923 = 58024, minus refunds 9480 + 23129 = 32609, which leaves 25415. Next I'll check birch, which has no refunds.
Birch's net of 30973 matches my own check: orders 19628 + 11345 = 30973, with no refunds. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance, which has refund 30660 applied against it.

Cobalt's net of 33028 matches my own check: orders 36677 + 27011 = 63688, minus refund 30660 leaves 33028. The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff, and all three customers reconcile, so there is no reason to hold. I'll record acme's payout first.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch and cobalt both reconciled against my own arithmetic, so I'll record birch's payout next.
Acme and birch are recorded, and cobalt's net of 33028 reconciled against my own arithmetic, so I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts are recorded and each matched my own arithmetic, so the batch is complete and I'll close it out with the payout totals.
